request.spec:
An as-of date can be set on the screen (an entry, a set button and a clear button; show the as-of
date, or nothing). While it is set, every cell on the screen for the signed-in user (every figure,
flag, list and line: in every row, every total, the header, the periods, the rates, the summary, and
any panel added later unless its request says otherwise) is shown as it stood at the end of the last
day on or before that date: every change made while the sheet's today was on or before the as-of
date counts, every later change does not, and the as-of date stands in for the sheet's today in
every figure (overdue, late charges, holds, deferrals, retirements, the grade and rate in force).
The audit file is unaffected, and every change, a statement as of a date included, is refused with
its usual error while the as-of date is set. The as-of date belongs to the signed-in user's screen;
other users are unaffected.

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The as-of view is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works**
- **On screen:** a new header form has the date entry (`asof-date`), a set button (`asof-set`) and a clear button (`asof-clear`), and shows the date in `sheet-asof` (empty when none is set). The date lives in the URL (`asOf`), so it belongs to that user's screen only. Other users are unaffected and it survives a sheet reload.
- **Reading data:** every read the screen makes passes `asOf` to the server and is cached separately for that date. On the server, the sheet, people, claims, periods, rates, settings, watches, roles and delegations endpoints accept an optional `?asOf=`. When it's given, each one returns its data as it stood at the end of that date, using the existing history tables. The as-of date also replaces the sheet's today: `useSheetToday` returns it, so overdue, late charges, holds, deferrals, retirements and the grade and rate in force all follow it. The `sheet-today` cell still shows the real today.
- **More history:** migration `V40__as_of_view.sql` adds history for statements, periods and their fixed totals, patrons, watches, roles and delegations, using the existing `HistoryTrigger`. It also records the date a sheet was archived, so "archived" can be shown as of a date.
- **Changes are refused:** while a date is set, every change the screen sends carries an `X-As-Of` header. A new server filter, `sheet/AsOfGuard.java`, rejects any non-read `/api/` request with that header before it reaches an endpoint. Each form then shows its usual error, and nothing is written to the store or the audit file. A statement taken as of a date is refused the same way.

**One fix outside the request:** the date entry for "statement as of a date" kept its value after a refused submission, so the next plain statement reused the bad date and was refused too. Scenario 2 failed on this. The entry now clears every time a statement is submitted.

**Not covered:** only data created after this migration runs has history for the newly tracked tables. Statements, periods, patrons and so on that already existed have no history rows, so an as-of view won't show them. With the in-memory database the app uses now, this only matters if the database ever becomes persistent.

**Worth knowing:** while debugging I found that when a read endpoint hits an SQL error, the server returns 200 with an empty body and logs nothing. That's how the app already behaved, and I didn't change it, but it makes failures like that hard to spot.
